newsitem.title: ITALY: SURVEY-Italy to ease by end-96 but lira wild card.
newsitem.headline: SURVEY-Italy to ease by end-96 but lira wild card.

text.p: The Bank of Italy will cut its discount rate by 50 basis points by the end of the year because economic fundamentals justify such a move, but the timing is uncertain due to the lira's likely ERM return, economists said.

In a survey of 12 international economists conducted by Reuters on Friday, all 12 saw further rate cuts in the offing and more than half expected the central bank would ease the key discount rate by the first week of December.
The Bank of Italy last cut its key discount and fixed term advances or Lombard rates by 75 basis points to 7.5 and 9.0 percent on October 23.

Six Italian sample cities published preliminary inflation data for November on Thursday which showed prices running at 2.6 percent year-on-year compared with 3.0 in October, and a month-on-month rate of 0.2 percent against a prior 0.1 percent.
But analysts do not rule out the year-on-year rate may come in at 2.5 percent when four more cities publish their data after 1630 GMT on Friday. Final November CPI is due on December 5.
"This is a level which justifies a rate cut even before the final data," said Marco Pianelli at Nomura.

But economists said the Bank of Italy had to take account of the likely return of the lira to Europe's exchange rate mechanism, after a report that Prime Minister Romano Prodi had said a return was imminent and after sources said a European monetary committee meeting was a near certainty this weekend.

Some saw the central bank waiting until after re-entry, as this looked imminent and the central bank would want to avoid excess pressures on the currency. Others said however the central bank would want to cut while still outside the system.

1 - Will there be another cut in interest rates?

The following participated: Banca di Roma, Bank of America, Banco di Sardegna, Caboto, BCI, San Paolo Bank, Chase Manhattan, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Nomura, CSFB and one other which asked not to be quoted.
